framing_note: This limitation set is intentionally bounded. It shows 6 representative weak points observed on the canonical showcase pages without turning the analysis into an exhaustive failure catalogue. Each case is phrased in a thesis-credible, bounded way.

cases.short_note: Language detection drifts away from Old English on the grammatical page, likely because the training distribution underrepresents insular script; full-page OCR remains contentful despite misidentification.
Insular abbreviation marks (macrons, Tironian nota) are preserved in raw OCR output but are not expanded to full word forms; a dedicated normalisation pass would be needed for downstream NLP.
Narrow upper-page heading regions and short decorated lines produce noisier OCR than the stronger main text bands; the layout model occasionally merges adjacent short regions.
The Abaton page is detected as Catalan rather than Latin; the OCR transcript remains coherent enough for semantic extraction despite the language misidentification.

cases.limitation_type: weak entity extraction on non-entity pages
cases.short_note: Entity extraction surfaces common doctrinal nouns ('seigneur', 'nature') as candidate mentions but correctly refrains from linking them to authority records; on pages with genuine named entities, this conservatism may under-recall.

cases.limitation_type: unsupported inference risk avoided or reduced by grounding
cases.short_note: Grounding pipeline correctly avoids asserting authority links for theological and moral vocabulary, reducing the risk of unsupported scholarly claims; this conservative strategy is safer than over-linking on doctrinal pages.
